title: Search log capture at investigation time (foundational)
description: Signature original: During the original investigation, every query, source version, and retrieval parameter is captured into a replay log. Capture is automatic and complete; a replay is only as good as the log it replays. The log format is stable across tool versions so old investigations stay replayable. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).

print('captured steps:', len(replay_log))

title: Query replay against pinned versions (foundational)
description: Signature original: Replay re-issues each logged query against the same source versions recorded in the log, not the current live versions. Pinning versions isolates the search procedure from archive drift: if the replay diverges, the cause is the procedure, not changed data. Where a pinned version is unavailable, the replay notes the substitution explicitly. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
log = [{'q': 'index latency', 'src_ver': 'v12'}]
for step in log:
    print(f"replaying '{step['q']}' against pinned {step['src_ver']}")
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Research Reproduction Tool, 2026-10-21.

title: Source-version availability check (foundational)
description: Signature original: Before replaying, the tool checks that every pinned source version is still retrievable. Missing versions are reported up front with their identifiers, so the replay can degrade gracefully instead of failing halfway. This check is what makes 'where possible' in the tool's mandate operational rather than aspirational. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).

title: Result diffing: original vs replay (foundational)
description: Signature original: Original and replayed result sets are compared with Jaccard similarity over record identifiers, and rank changes are measured for the top positions. High similarity means the search reproduces; divergence is localized to the specific steps where it appears. The diff distinguishes procedure instability from data drift by consulting the version-pinning notes. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
def jacc(a, b):
    A, B = set(a), set(b)
    return len(A & B) / max(1, len(A | B))
orig, replay = ['d1', 'd2', 'd3', 'd4'], ['d1', 'd3', 'd2', 'd5']
print('replay similarity:', round(jacc(orig, replay), 2))
print('verdict:', 'REPRODUCES' if jacc(orig, replay) >= 0.75 else 'DIVERGES -> investigate')
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Research Reproduction Tool, 2026-10-21.

title: Replay report with divergence analysis (foundational)
description: Signature original: The replay ends in a report: per-step similarity, overall verdict, and for each divergence whether the cause looks like procedure, data drift, or version substitution. The report is stored alongside the original investigation so future readers know how reproducible the search was. Honest divergence notes are more valuable than a forced 'reproduces' stamp. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
